about: What's new, shown once when the app opens (whats-new.js). Hand-edited: add one short plain line at the TOP of items for each change people will notice, with today's date. Newest first.

items.text: The app runs out of memory less often on iPhone: a little while after you switch back to the flat map, the hidden 3D map lets go of its memory, and saving offline maps uses less.
Save ride: no more save page. Save puts the ride straight into My rides and you stay on the map; add a name or photos later from My rides.
Skiing 3D: your trails, routes and the tour you're planning stay on the map when you come back to the app.
Skiing: switching the 3D map off and back on no longer freezes the app.
Skiing: the avalanche forecast now comes live from Avalanche Canada every time you open the app, so a new or updated bulletin shows right away.
Skiing avalanche forecast: never shows yesterday's day as today, refreshes when you come back to the app, and warns when you're looking at an old saved copy.
Opening the app for the first time is lighter and quicker, especially in Skiing.
Planning a ski tour is faster: your tour and its less exposed way show up sooner.
Skiing avalanche shading: every slope now shows exactly Avalanche Canada's rating for its band, and slopes facing today's problems are a darker shade (darker yellow at Moderate) instead of stripes.
Skiing: freeride lines are now black on a white edge, so they no longer look like the pink-red slackcountry lines.
Same line icons for every sport everywhere in the app, and Adventure moto now has its own dirt bike icon.
Account Settings: a green ✓ box now confirms when your password, name or email change worked.
Skiing avalanche forecast explained: each problem in plain words, what its size means, and Avalanche Canada's own advice.
Skiing opens with touring routes, snowmobile trails, webcams, lift status and slackcountry when you're not signed in.
Skiing 3D map moves smoothly again near Squamish, Whistler and Kicking Horse.
Skiing webcams: the Black Tusk Snowmobile Club's 4 live cameras at the Brohm Ridge chalet, above Squamish (they run in winter).
Hunting: a layer that isn't mapped in your province now says so, Alberta grazing leases show in Alberta, and range ring labels no longer pile up when zoomed out.
Share a spot with a friend: every This spot card has a Share button. Your friend gets a link that opens the app on that spot with a purple pin, plus the coordinates.
Skiing Ask: "the end of Brandywine Meadows tomorrow" starts where the forest road meets the snow line and uses tomorrow's avalanche forecast.
Account: tapping Create an account opens its own screen, and a new account is ready right away (no email to wait for).

Skiing: the Powder Mountain Snowmobile Club's sled trails at Brandywine are on the map: Brandywine Bowl, Metal Dome, Chocolate Bowl, and the backcountry routes to Powder Mountain, the Sea of White and Ring Mountain.
Adventure moto: the Mud and dust today squares are off the map. The Dirt today card and Mud today button stay.
Skiing: Plan a new tour and Saved tours are now at the top of Routes, next to Plan a tour.
Skiing: planning a tour takes fewer taps. Each tour is saved by itself, and a typed plan can be made with the less exposed way in one tap.
Skiing: save a planned tour (★ Save this tour) and start another; saved tours are in Saved and on your account.
Skiing 3D: the winter photo is sharper and cleaner from the middle distance at Whistler, Revelstoke, Rogers Pass and Kicking Horse, without the grey squares.
Skiing opens with Lift status and Slackcountry on; Your ski tours are a switch in Layers.
One search bar for everything: type a place or ask in plain words, and Go turns into Ask when it reads like a question.
3D map: trail and route lines are sharp now, drawn on top of the mountains instead of painted soft into the photo.
Skiing Plan a tour: type your plan in words (start, lines, finish) and it draws the tour.
Terms of use now cover every sport and every feature, including ones added later. You'll tap I agree once more.
Skiing Ask: the Duffey (“the duffys” too) and every backcountry area by name, with all their tours, plus Anniversary Glacier and Vantage Peak from Keith's Hut.
The app opens faster, most of all when you open it again
Photo find: when your picture matches one riders took of a trail, that trail comes first, and parts of one trail (like Gouranga and Gouranga Rock Ride) show together.
Cabin trips: the way in now starts at the hut's winter parking, follows its winter route, and shows closures (Keith's Hut and more).
Skiing tours: clearer steep-slope notes, progress while finding a way, readable danger.
3D turns smoothly on a computer, and the sharp snow photos come in seconds sooner when you zoom in close.

Skiing: Safest way is now Less exposed way, turned on for each tour. Each tour starts with today's avalanche danger, no way is drawn at High or Extreme danger or with no forecast, and the avalanche warning comes back each winter.
Skiing: the Safest way no longer puts advice tags (One at a time, Don't stop) or regroup pins on the map. The route and its Watch out list show the terrain; how to travel it is your call.
3D opens sooner: "Loading the mountains" goes as soon as the mountains are drawn, and the sharp photos fill in while you look.
Privacy page now in French too, says where your data is kept and for how long, and More has a switch to stop sharing how you use the app.
Skiing opens faster with fewer layers on: touring routes, approaches, parking and lift status. Turn on the rest in Layers; on Rogers Pass the app asks to show the permit areas.
Skiing 3D map moves more smoothly: pins far off the screen no longer slow down every move.
Routes never double back: a tour, ride, hike or drive no longer goes up to a spot and comes back the same way (Corona Bowl and other Blackcomb lines fixed).
Skiing: tap a point or step in your tour list to see it up close, facing it.

Terms of use: you agree once before using the app that you make your own decisions and take the risk, and the terms now spell out what the Safest way, ATES classes, weather, route status and GPS tracks can and can't tell you.

Skiing: the Safest way weighs time spent on or under avalanche slopes (it drops to flat ground and climbs back rather than sidehilling) and today's new snow, wind, rain and warming, marks One at a time and Don't stop spots, and shows green R places to regroup.
Skiing: the Poop Chutes now go down the Phalanx Glacier like the GPS track (not the north ridge), and Whistler Blackcomb's 21 official uphill and backcountry routes show today's Open or Closed.
Skiing: Phalanx via the Stairmaster bootpack, the real way to the top of the Poop Chutes, and tours to there follow it (no more Phalanx south ridge, which has rock pinnacles).
Skiing: ＋ Add a point under End in your tour's list, then tap the map where you want to go next.
Skiing: every new tour starts with the 🛡 Safest way on, and Ask reads "the bottom of Poop Chutes on Glacier Road" as Poop Chutes, by Glacier Road.
Skiing Ask: knows every chairlift by name, even misspelled ("finish at the bottom of 7th even" is the 7th Heaven chair).
Skiing: a tour plan typed in the search box ("start at the top of Showcase, ski DOA, finish in Lakeside Bowl") now goes to Ask and becomes a tour.

Skiing: type your plan of the day in Ask ("start at the top of Showcase, ski DOA, finish in Lakeside Bowl") and it makes the tour on the map, with the 🛡 Safest way for the climb and what it is based on.
Skiing: while you plan or show a tour, the other lines get thinner and fainter and their names smaller, so your route stands out.

Less crowded maps: smaller slackcountry and freeride names in Skiing with no names on top of each other or twice, fewer trail names in 3D, and fewer piled-up dots in Hiking and Adventure moto. Hiking now writes the hike names on the map, like MTB.
Fishing: Green Lake (Whistler) now shows its signed boat zones on the map (no-wake ends, waterski middle, float plane landing) and the sign's rules and report numbers in Boating.
Directions stay in the app now, like Google Maps: add stops, pick Drive, Bike or Walk, then Start for turn-by-turn with the next turn on top, spoken turns and the map following you.

Adventure moto: Directions stay in the app now: add stops, pick Moto, Bike or Walk, then Start for turn-by-turn like Apple Maps, with the next turn on top, spoken turns, the map following you, and a dark look after sunset.

Layers: Forest roads and Wildfires now show their status under the name: how many km of road in view are good, rough, closed or impassable, and how many fires within 100 km are out of control, being held or under control. Fire pins are red, orange or yellow by status.
Skiing Plan a tour: turning 🛡 Safest on and off is instant now; the line, distance and steepest slope switch together.
Offline maps for Hiking: an area saved in Hiking keeps its hiking trails and terrain, so you can plan a hike with no signal (the route follows the trails, with its climb and height profile).
Skiing Plan a tour: your tour is only on the map while you plan or edit it, or after Show on map (Hide from map takes it off); zoomed out it's just the line, without its numbered points.
Offline maps now need a free account: tap Save and you'll be asked to sign in first, then the save starts. Maps you already saved keep working with no signal.
Skiing Safest way: the route no longer breaks off near your points (each piece now starts and ends right on them), and Your route shows the same distance and climb as the summary above it.
Skiing Plan a tour: the list of your points (Start, 1, 2 … End) is always shown under Undo and Clear, with the safest way on or off, so you can reorder or delete points any time.

Hiking: every hiking trail in Canada now loads ready-made, so Quebec, Ontario and the East show all their hikes right away (no more waiting on “Finding more hiking trails”), including trails mapped as tracks like Sentier de la Montagne Noire.
Hiking: trails are easier to see on the map and in 3D (white edge, the open hike bold), and well-known hikes with no grade on the map now get one from a hiking guide.
Skiing Plan a tour: drag the end of a line you added along it and the line stops there; your tour goes on to the next point from that spot.

Skiing Plan a tour is easier: the bar says what to tap next, drag any point to move it (flat map and 3D), Undo takes back any change, and tapping a freeride line or slackcountry route while planning offers to add the whole line.
Hiking: hike cards now show real photos of the hike when free-to-use ones exist (credited, tap to see them big).

Sea to Sky trails checked against local sources: Squamish trails get the District of Squamish’s own grades, SORCA’s 2025-26 trail work shows on each trail, and Whistler’s alpine hiking trails no longer show as bike trails.

Ontario logging: with Logging areas on, Ontario's own plans now show the blocks set to be logged this year (gold) and the ones logged lately (pink); tap one for the cut type. Skiing also has 43 more live webcams in Quebec, Ontario and the Maritimes (Tremblant, Bromont, Saint-Sauveur, Mont-Saint-Louis, the Chic-Chocs...) and live lifts at Owl's Head, Horseshoe, Mont Sainte-Marie and Searchmont.
Photo find is simpler: the “Teach it your trails” section is gone. Photo find still learns from every Yes you give it.
Cleaner look: one style of icons everywhere, a Key in Hiking, and the Record tab named the same in Skiing, Hunting, Fishing and Hiking.
Area not on the list? Pick “Type another town or area…” at the bottom of the Area list and type any town or riding area in Canada, like Cumberland. New trails and trail name searches then look there.
Skiing Plan a tour: tap Add to tour on a line's card (a freeride line or any route) and your tour skis that exact line from its top to its bottom.

Before your first tour, off-trail route or planned route, a short note makes clear that you make your own decisions and go at your own risk, with a line under every route. The Terms of use say it in full.
Skiing Plan a tour: delete a point with the × beside it in Your route; the safest way is found again without it.

Skiing Plan a tour: the route's points (Start, 1, 2 ... End) and its !n watch-out spots now show on the 3D map too, you can move points up or down in the list or reverse the tour, the route line is bolder, and the map no longer stalls while a long tour is worked out.
Skiing Safest way has a cleaner, calmer look: route totals at the top, a compact step list, fewer colours, and Why this way and Watch out fold away until you tap them.

Skiing Safest way follows the forecast: the way up always takes the safest line, and the ski down is more direct at Low or Moderate danger, the safest one when it's High or Extreme. Planning a tour no longer turns on slope angles.
Skiing Plan a tour: 🛡 Safest way is on by default, and the route shows as a list like MTB's (skin up, ski down, the named tracks it takes) and sticks to mapped skin tracks.
Skiing Safest way: the route now has a step list (Start, Point 1, 2 ... End) with each leg's distance, climb and why, matching labels on the map, and it no longer runs down plowed highways.
When you save something or turn on an alert without an account, a small card offers to sign in so it's on all your devices. You can say Not now.
Skiing: the Duffey classics Chief Pascall and Cayoosh (Kayoosh) are now ski tours, and Ask lists the classics first.
Skiing: 🛡 Safest way plans a tour around avalanche terrain (slope angle, today's forecast and problem aspects, slopes above and terrain traps) and shows why on the route.
Skiing This spot: the terrain box (Simple, Challenging, Complex) is now easy to read and fits in its box.
Skiing Freeride lines no longer show marked runs like Insanity and Powerline at Whistler Creekside.
Plan a hike still finds a route along the trails when the route server is busy, and a new Data credits page lists every source.
Privacy: photo search no longer lets anyone see when other people confirmed a picture of a trail.
Search finds trails by their old name too, and a trail keeps its name when the map loses it.
Radar forecast now looks like Skiing's: smooth and see-through, snow in purples and rain in greens, with the same colours in every sport.
Radar: slide past Latest (or tap Next 3 days) to see where rain or snow is forecast over the next 3 days, plus a 3-day total.
Sign out now removes your saved trails, folders, rides and pins from that device (they stay safe in your account), so the next person using it never sees them.
MTB: unofficial trails (the ones only approved riders see dotted) are no longer shown to everyone else.
Account: sign in with a code from the email (works in the iPhone app), add your name, and download all your data from Settings.
Fixed a rare error that could stop a trail from opening when some of its map details were missing.
Sign out is now a button right in the Account box, next to Done.

Trail search stays in the Area you picked, even a whole region like Sea to Sky. A trail with the same name elsewhere in Canada is only listed after, clearly marked, and Search never jumps there by itself.
Skiing 3D: searching a place now turns the 3D map to the side it's seen best from, so ridges in front don't hide it.
Searching a place now frames it close so you really see it: a backcountry area like Sky Pilot fills the screen, above the bottom sheet on phones, and 3D looks at it less tilted.
MTB: trails mapped as closed, private or not open to bikes are no longer shown, out of respect for land owners and local trail builders.
Skiing: far fewer cloudy, painted-in patches in the sharp Winter photos at Kicking Horse, Rogers Pass and Revelstoke.
Skiing: the Sea to Sky Gondola is on the map as the way up to Sky Pilot. Tap it for today's hours, if skis can go up, the groomed access road, routes, webcams and parking.
Search: places now show as you type in every sport (towns, mountains, lakes, parks, resorts, routes, huts, trails), even with a typo like “revol” for Revelstoke.
Skiing: sharper Winter photos up close at Revelstoke, Rogers Pass and Kicking Horse too.
Skiing: the sharper Winter photos around Whistler load faster in 3D.
Searching a place now takes the map much closer: a ski resort fills the screen, a town shows its streets (2D and 3D, every sport).
Skiing: route cards now show length, climb, descent, time, top and bottom in boxes, with the height profile right under them.

Skiing: uphill ski routes (skin tracks) at Quebec hills now show as backcountry ski routes with their own card (Mont Sutton's Piste d'Ascension and Skimo), and more Chic-Chocs ski lines (Mont Lyall, the Cuves de la Mine, Mont Porphyre, Mont Hog's Back, the Grande Cuve).
Skiing: sharper Winter photos around Squamish, Whistler and Pemberton when you zoom in close, sharpened 4 times by a free AI model (2D and 3D).
Skiing: 9 more slackcountry runs at Whistler Blackcomb (Flute back side, Oboe east, Fissile, Circle Lake, Spearhead Glacier, Phalanx, Decker Glacier, Disease Ridge, Spearhead Traverse).
Skiing: the search box is now at the top, and shows resorts, routes, huts, freeride and slackcountry lines and towns as you type.
Skiing: a route or freeride line card only shows a photo at the top when the photo is really of that line. Nearby photos stay under Photos.
Skiing: hut cards show a photo of the hut when there is a free one online, or a link to the club's photos.
Skiing: Joffre Shoulder on the Duffey is now a ski tour, with where to park, the climb and what to watch for.

Skiing: snow stations near Bromont, Mont-Tremblant, the Chic-Chocs, Blue Mountain, Sugarloaf and Marble Mountain (now shown even before the snow), the nearest avalanche forecast where none covers you (Whitehorse), and a ski heatmap shortcut where no tour is mapped.

Skiing: new Freeride lines layer (Layers, Resorts): the named chutes, couloirs, faces and glades skiers have mapped, not the groomed runs. About 100 at Whistler Blackcomb and about 1,450 across Canada (resorts, heli and cat skiing, Baffin Island). Tap one for its steepness, drop and which way it faces.
Skiing: the flat map has a new Winter style (Layers), last winter's satellite photos with snow, the same as the 3D map. It opens on Winter in Skiing.
Hiking: Today shows which hikes near you are snow-free, Plan a hike follows the trails, plus trailheads, huts, viewpoints, water and slope angle in Layers, and a height profile on each hike.
Skiing: 6 more huts on the map with booking, price and beds: Mt. Colin and Castle Mountain (Rockies), Raven Lake, Grizzly Den and 8 Mile (near Prince George) and Wally Joyce (Bon Echo, Ontario).
3D map is sharper close up on phones when the map is still and not tilted far, with no extra memory.
3D map Live is now a real recent satellite photo (with its date), so it shows today's snow or bare ground, not the Summer photo again.
Cleaner look: fewer names on the map, a calmer map style, a simpler trail card, and one search box that also takes questions.
New sport: 🥾 Hiking. Hikes by grade, time and heights, snow at the top today, the park pass it needs, and closures nearby.
Trail reports, rider photos and rider grades have ⚑ Report and Hide this rider. New Terms and safety page in More.
Photo find, Ask in plain words and fish ID now ask once before anything goes to Google's AI (18 or older). Change it in More, Google's AI.
More real trail grades: Vernon (Kal Park, Ellison, Predator, King Eddy) from the City of Vernon trail map, Kimberley Nature Park from its society's map, and Fireman at China Ridge.
3D map on iPhone: it now gives back all its memory while you are in another app, to stop the restarts when you come back. The 3D map redraws for a second or two when you return.

Hunting, Fishing and Moto: the place search now suggests towns as you type. Fishing: Where to fish today knows the season (cold water, ice likely). Moto: the same campground shows once, and the Sport button says Moto.

Skiing: Whistler webcams no longer pile up in the village, Ski touring lists real tours before plain loops, smaller phones fit the sheet better, map buttons are easier to tap, and Skiing opens faster by skipping bike trail files.
Prime loam: when no trail is prime, it now lists the trails closest to prime instead of an empty list, and a trail rated differently along its length shows the whole range (Blue to Black) everywhere.
3D map: uses less memory when you leave the app or go back to the flat map, and the snow forecast redraws more calmly, to stop the 3D restarts on iPhone.
Japan: Hokkaido Wilds ski tours and huts in Hokkaido, snow depth at the weather stations, and Japan's official topo map.
Offline maps: your saved areas are outlined on the map with no signal (2D and 3D), Skiing saves blurry winter photos all around them, and the square to save can't grow past the size limit.
Save an area for no signal without planning a route: Saved → Offline maps, or Layers → Save this area offline, in every sport, 2D and 3D.

Skiing webcams: live video now plays right in the card on iPhone, a big Open the live stream button, and a clear note with the last picture when a camera is off. Every cam checked: Kicking Horse videos and Big White pictures fixed.
Trail levels: 10 Banff trails now show Parks Canada's level and 5 Mount Swansea trails (Invermere) the Columbia Valley tourism level.
Find: tap 📍 Looking in to type any town or riding area in Canada, use Near me, or pick from recent and popular areas, instead of the long list.
Map: your location dot now stays put when you zoom in or out while the map follows you, and a pinch keeps the spot under your fingers.
Japan: 🔊 on each Japanese phrase says it out loud, and winter satellite photos for Hakuba, Myoko, Nozawa, Hokkaido and Hakkoda in the 3D map.
3D map: town, peak and lake names in Japan (and anywhere not written in our letters) now show in English.
iPhone app: the New version popup now shows as soon as a newer build is ready in TestFlight.

Skiing in Japan: runs, lifts, tours and huts everywhere, the Japan Avalanche Network's daily danger for Hakuba, Myoko and Hokkaido, backcountry areas, and camper van stops (Michi-no-eki, RV parks, onsen, ferries), and 🗣 Japanese help: phrases to show people, emergency numbers and Translate.
Skiing 3D on iPhone: fixed black squares on the ground after moving around for a while.
Français : the app is now in French on phones set to French (Quebec). Switch it any time in More, Language / Langue.
Forest roads across Canada now show each road's government status (open, closed, maintained, drivable) in BC, Yukon, Ontario, Quebec and Nova Scotia. Lake Louise's bike trails are on the map.
Search finds trails riders added, and when a trail isn't on the map at all you can add it right from the search.
Skiing huts: 7 more on the map (Tom's Hut with how to get in on skis, Jacques Lake, Mt. Alberta, Journeyman Lodge, Woodbury, Knuckleheads, Naiset), and exact prices for the Alpine Club huts.
Maps you've seen are kept on your phone, so the map and the 3D ground show right away next time. Skiing opens lighter, and pins on top of each other in 3D wait until you zoom in.
iPhone app (next update): in MTB, Layers > Native map (test) opens a map drawn by the iPhone itself. Try it and tell us if it moves smoother.

Eastern Canada: live lift status at 7 more hills (Stoneham, Le Massif, Sutton, Orford, Val Saint-Côme, Le Relais, Mount St. Louis), lift lines at 25 eastern hills, 60 road cams near eastern hills, and Ontario and New Brunswick forest roads with gates.
Skiing cabin trips: day tours from the cabin, a packing list made for your trip, and a trip plan to send a friend with a late alert for their calendar.
Signed in: cabin trips, watched tours, moto routes and bikes now follow you to every device.
Tap or drag anywhere on the map (2D or 3D) and it stops following you. Tap Recenter (or Follow while riding) to follow again.
Skiing cabin trips: the card now says Not finished when some offline files are still missing, and Saved only when it all is.
Offline maps: Pick a square shows a square right away with big corners to drag, and a big green Saved or orange Not saved box says if it worked. Missing files are tried again by themselves.
Skiing cabin trips: the way in now starts where the road is plowed, and unplowed logging roads count as part of the ski in.
How it works is much shorter: one or two lines per feature, opening on your sport's part.

Skiing: huts show as brown house pins when you zoom in, with a green “Book” tag when they must be booked. Tap one to see the price, beds, heat and water, and a Book button that opens the club's booking page.
Skiing: plan a cabin trip. Tap a hut, then 🏕 Plan a cabin trip here: pick your dates, see the easiest way in from the parking, the avalanche danger and weather for each day, and save it all offline.
Skiing: tap a hut and its card pops up right away, and hut names show beside the dots when you zoom in close.
Skiing 3D no longer runs out of memory with Snow and rain forecast or the radar on: the 3D map now frees the old pictures each time those layers update.
3D map in every sport: a soft photo shows right away after you move or zoom out, instead of blank ground or holes to the sky while the sharp photos load.
Skiing 3D: the ground fills in faster after you move, with a soft winter photo instead of grey patches while the sharp one loads.
The map Key button now moves up above the radar, clouds and smoke bars on phones, so it no longer sits on top of their colour key.
Faster on phones: typing a trail name in search no longer freezes the keyboard, and zooming out over new trails stays smoother.
Skiing: Snow forecast and New snow also show rain (in greens) where it rains instead, make the 3D map lag less, and no longer leave dark patches when the weather service is busy.
Skiing: the Whistler snow stake cam now plays the live video (it was a picture that refreshed each minute).
Skiing: the Whistler snow stake cam now shows the live picture of the new snow stake (it showed an old summer picture before).
3D map: pins for far-away places (webcams, huts, lifts, ski areas, parking) no longer float in the sky above the mountains. Pins on slopes you can see stay put.

Skiing 3D: Snow forecast and New snow now colour the whole view, far distance included. Before, wide views asked the weather service for too much at once and some squares stayed bare (dark patches) for an hour.

Layers that colour the whole ground (Avalanche risk, Slope angle, New snow, Snow forecast, Forest types, Mud and more) now show one at a time: turning one on turns the other off, so the map stays readable and lighter on your phone.

Skiing: tap anywhere and the This spot card now shows the snow that fell in the last 24 h, 3 days and 7 days, the snow forecast for the next 24 h, 3 days and 7 days, and the weather day by day for the past week and the week ahead. New snow and Snow forecast now turn each other off, so only one shows at a time.
Skiing: the Whistler snow stake cam is on the map with the other Whistler Blackcomb webcams, so you can see how much new snow fell.
Hunting: drop pins and tag them: trail cam, tracks, saline, cache, stand, rub, scrape, bait, kill site, parking, other and more. A pin can have several tags, and Saved filters your pins by tag.
Hunting: the map no longer freezes when you zoom out over a whole province, and zone names no longer pile on top of each other.

Hunting: new Property lines layer shows the lines between lots (Quebec cadastre, BC, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia; Ontario lots and concessions, Alberta sections). Zoom in close and tap a spot for the lot number.
Fishing: creeks and streams now show from a whole-valley zoom, Crown land works in BC (private land in yellow), and tapping a BC lake gives its scanned depth map.

Yukon: hunting seasons for every game management subzone (tap the map in Hunting), and fishing limits for each Yukon lake and river with its own rules, like Fish Lake, Lake Laberge and the Yukon River at Whitehorse.
Photo find asks where a picture was taken when only the AI guessed the place, then compares it with riders' pictures of every trail there.
Skiing 3D: the mountains come up about twice as fast when you open it, and the 3D map uses less of your phone's memory so it runs out less.

Live lift status at Revelstoke, Lake Louise, RED Mountain and Mont-Sainte-Anne, lake depths in Alberta (169 lakes) and Nova Scotia (634 lake maps), and backcountry ski cards for Fish Lake near Whitehorse and the Tablelands in Gros Morne.
The app opens faster: Skiing, Hunting, Fishing and Moto now load only when you pick them.
Real trail ratings for Fernie, the Cranbrook Community Forest and Penticton's Three Blind Mice, from the local trail clubs' and regional district's own maps.
Search finds towns and trails anywhere in Canada: type Bromont and the map goes there.
Trail heights now load even when the weather service is busy, and shuttle routes warn you about gates to check (🚧).
New trails now shows the list right away, the app finds you even if you skip the welcome, and Prime loam tells you which day the dirt turns prime when nothing is prime today.
3D winter photos now cover Cumberland, Prince George, Whitehorse and Hardwood too.
Ski heatmap: much more around Whistler, the Spearhead and the Callaghan. Slackcountry past the resort gates is no longer cut out, and tours recorded with fewer GPS points now count.
Fishing and Hunting in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Newfoundland and Labrador: fishing areas with their rules, and hunting seasons for each zone.
Skiing webcams: the Brandywine Bowl sled cam near Whistler, four Coquihalla sled cams (parking lot to the 10-K cabin), and alpine station cams at Plummer Hut, Klinaklini and the Cruickshank valley.
Sharper satellite map in Ontario and around Lake Louise, Sunshine and Banff: the province's and the park's own air photos.
Logging areas now work everywhere in Canada: outside BC, Alberta and Quebec they show forest cut or burned since 2010, seen from space.
Skiing: live lift status at Tremblant, Blue Mountain and Bromont.
Skiing webcams: live highway cameras near Smithers, Whitehorse, Sugarloaf, Wentworth, Blue Mountain and Marble, and Mont-Sainte-Anne's 6 cameras in the app.
Fishing: Layers has picture tiles to highlight all rivers, all lakes, creeks, the ocean, lake depths and Crown land, on the flat and 3D map.
Find: tap 📍 under the search box to change area; no match looks in all areas.
Loops: after opening a loop on the map, tap ← Loops to go back to the same list and pick another.
iPhone app: loam, avalanche and stocking alerts now arrive as real iPhone notifications.
iPhone app: while you record, your time, km, climb and the trail you're on show on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island.
iPhone app: a popup tells you when a newer version is ready in TestFlight.
